backPrompt:
BACK PRINT of the shirt, and it is a DESIGN IN ITS OWN RIGHT - never the front motif copied and parked at the top.
Build it like the back of a tour shirt, where the list of names IS the star of the show and the artwork frames it:
- TOP: the main text "{motto}" as a big arched headline, and the signature character or icon of the front is WOVEN INTO it - peeking over the top edge of the letters, sitting on them, holding them, or reaching around them. Never a separate picture stacked above the word.
- Directly under the headline a wide OPENING ornament spanning most of the width: a rule with stars, a striped bar, a ribbon or a burst - whatever fits the art style. It announces the list.
- THE WHOLE MIDDLE STAYS COMPLETELY EMPTY. No text, no names, no boxes, no lines, no ornaments, nothing - a list of names is typeset there afterwards.
- LEFT and RIGHT of that empty middle, a few LOOSE, separate small pieces in the art style (stars, a trail, a small symbol of the front) with bare fabric between them - never a continuous column, never a band, no wider than one tenth of the canvas each. They accompany the list without ever entering it.
- NO FRAME, NO BOX, NO PLATE: the top, the sides and the bottom NEVER join into a closed rectangle or border around the names. Top and bottom stand free, the side pieces stop well before them, and the bare fabric runs in between everywhere - on the shirt the back reads as headline, names and a closing banner, never as a panel or sign with an edge.
- BOTTOM: a closing element under the names, not connected to the sides - a badge, a banner or a crest[[ showing "{schule}"]][[ and "{ort}"]]. Small and wide, not a second main motif.
The empty middle is at least half the height of the canvas. Same art style, palette and technique as the front, but a different composition - someone looking at front and back must see two designs of one family, not the same picture twice.

Lettering - every text exactly as given, nothing else:
- The title "{titel}" is the dominant headline in big, heavy letters.
- The team name "{team}" in strong lettering right with it.
- The season or year "{saison}" is a LARGE element - on German championship shirts the year is always big and clearly visible, never a small footnote.
[[- A banner or line reads exactly "{liga}".]]
[[- A line with a bold upward arrow reads exactly "{aufstieg_in}" - the promotion target.]]
[[- A curved line or ribbon near the bottom reads exactly "{spruch}".]]
No other words, no invented years or numbers.

The sport is {sportart}[[ - more precisely: {sportart_frei}]]. The motif is built from the typical equipment of exactly this sport (ball, puck, racket, bat, boat, bike, target, pins or gear) plus the classic triumph symbols: trophy cup, laurel, crown, star, confetti, winner's ribbon. Use only equipment that really belongs to this sport - pure ball sports only their ball plus goal, net or basket; racket and stick sports their racket, bat or stick with the matching ball or puck; strength and martial arts belt, gloves or mat; target sports target, arrows or darts. Never the equipment of a different sport. No real club crest, no league logo, no shield-shaped badge, no player faces.

Layout: the composition follows the variation given below - a classic German Meistershirt layout made fresh. Everything reads as ONE print: lettering and motif locked together, centred, big enough to read from across the pitch.

Style: bold championship poster print, thick outlines, gold and one strong team colour plus cream and black, halftone shading, no photorealism, no gradients.
